clauses.text:
By virtue o f and pursuant to the 
authority vested in me by paragraph 
Eighth, subdivision SECOND, section 2 
of the C ivil Service Act (22 Stat. 403, 
404), it is ordered that Subdivision IV  o f 
Schedule B o f the Civil Service Rules be, 
and it is hereby, amended by adding 
thereto the follow ing paragraph:
“ 5. Classified positions in  the Ord­
nance Department at Large, W ar De­
partment, when filled by the promotion |
o f unclassified laborers, subject to the 
approval o f the C ivil Service Commis­
sion.”
This order, which is recommended by 
the C ivil Service Commission in view of 
the agreement by the W ar Department 
that h ereafter unclassified laborer posi­
tions in the Ordnance Department at 
Large w ill be filled through appointment 
from  appropriate classified registers as 
provided in section 3 o f Civil Service 
Rule n , w ill perm it unskilled laborers 
appointed from  the unclassified laborer 
register to advance upon noncompeti­
tive examination to classified positions 
in the Ordnance Department at Large, 
but such promotion w ill not accord to 
such employees a classified status or 
render them eligible fo r transfer to clas­
sified positions in  other branches o f the 
Federal service.

status_research.rationale: I read the complete held EO 7980 (3 FR 2359, Oct. 4, 1938, signed Sept. 29, 1938; the held extract also carries EO 7981 on Civil Service Schedule B, which is a separate order): under sec. 22 of EO 6166 it orders that the transfers, consolidations and eliminations contemplated by sec. 4 of EO 6166, together with the operation of the other provisions of EO 6166 so far as they relate to sec. 4, 'be further delayed until December 31, 1938, with respect to the function of disbursement now exercised by United States Marshals under the Department of Justice'. It has no other operative clause, no extension mechanism and no savings clause. The cited TERM record (stated end 1938-12-31, kind until_event, scope EO:7980#whole) is taken from the app-executive-orders text copy; I checked that the identical words appear in the official Federal Register extract (fr-originals EO_7980.txt) and rely on that reading, not on the copy, which is never an original. On its own term the postponement stopped operating at the end of December 31, 1938, and nothing else in the order survives it. D6 self-check: the history has one observation (Amends: EO 6166) and no events. A search of all held texts for 7980 finds no amendment or extension of EO 7980 itself; later postponements of the same EO 6166 sec. 4 function were separate orders (not held under that wording), and EO 8455 (5 FR 2420, June 29, 1940) sec. 3 finally transferred the marshals' disbursement functions to the Department of Justice, which confirms the scheme was closed out. A later separate postponement could not revive EO 7980. Residual risk: whether an unheld order amended the date of EO 7980 rather than issuing a new postponement. Provisional NO hypothesis only.

Held EO 7980 (3 FR 2359, official FR text) has one command: the EO 6166 sec. 4 transfers relating to the marshals' disbursement function 'be further delayed until December 31, 1938'. Its own term ended that day; nothing else in the order survives. My status NO. Defect noted, status stands: the cited TERM record is taken from the APP transcription; I checked the identical wording in the official FR extract EO_7980.txt, which is the reading relied on. D6: no held order amends or extends EO 7980; the only held 6166 orders of 1938-40 are 7981 (same page), 8427/8428 and 8455 (which finally transfers the function), none reviving 7980. Accept, with defect.

record.rationale: Independent reading: held FR extract 3 FR 2359 (Oct. 4, 1938) prints '[No. 7980]' under the order 'Postponement of Effective Date of Certain Provisions of Executive Order No. 6166', which under EO 6166 sec. 22 delays the sec. 4 transfers 'until December 31, 1938, with respect to the function of disbursement now exercised by United States Marshals'; the next order on the page, [No. 7981], is the Schedule B civil-service amendment (the CLAUSES and condition TERM records wrongly attach EO 7981's text). My own status: NO by own term. The cited TERM record comes from the APP copy, but the identical words are in the official FR text, so the basis holds (defect: the basis id should point to an FR-derived record; APP is never an original). D6: no held order names EO 7980; EO 8455 (5 FR 2420) sec. 3 permanently vests the marshals' disbursement functions in Justice as of July 1, 1940, which shows intervening unheld postponements existed; whether one amended EO 7980's date rather than issuing a fresh postponement is unheld, but any such extension was closed out by EO 8455 sec. 3, so the clause is spent either way. Accept, with defect (APP-sourced basis id; mis-attributed CLAUSES record).

versions.research_rationale:
Executive Order 7980 of September 29, 1938, under section 22 of Executive Order 6166, further delays until December 31, 1938 the transfers, consolidations and eliminations contemplated by section 4 of Executive Order 6166 of June 10, 1933, as amended, and the operation of its other provisions so far as they relate to section 4, with respect to the disbursement function exercised by United States Marshals under the Department of Justice. The held Federal Register text (3 FR 2359) is a page that also prints the next order, Executive Order 7981 (Schedule B of the Civil Service Rules); the dossier's single clause spans the text of 7981, not of 7980, so the inventory is corrected to the 7980 text alone (characters 631 to 1751 of the held file, from the order heading through the Federal Register document line). The delay ends by its own terms on December 31, 1938, recorded inclusive under research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-until-and-further-exempt.md; the exclusive reading is the alternative. The packet's own-term evidence for this order points into the 7981 text and is not used; the end is read from the order's own sentence in the original evidence. The packet records no later event for 7980 (chain empty, OFR catalog zero hits); a postponement order in the same series would be a separate command and none is cited as a later event here because none is citable from this packet.
